learning_objective: 🎯 Develop an eagle eye! Learn the meticulous final step of the writing process to catch typos, grammatical errors, and formatting mistakes before publication.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Proofreading is the absolute last step before a text is published or submitted. Unlike editing (which changes sentences and structure), proofreading only looks for objective errors: spelling, grammar, and punctuation.

Spellcheck software is blind to homophones (words that sound the same but are spelled differently). A computer won't tell you if you mistakenly used 'their' instead of 'there', or 'affect' instead of 'effect'. Only a human proofreader can catch this!
A missing comma can change the entire meaning of a sentence! Proofreaders ensure commas, periods, quotation marks, and apostrophes are used correctly and consistently throughout the document.

Proofreaders check the visual elements. Are all the headings the same font size? Are the bullet points aligned? Is the line spacing consistent? A messy format makes even the best writing look unprofessional.

When we read our own writing, our brain 'auto-corrects' mistakes because it knows what we *meant* to say. Proofreaders use tricks like reading aloud or reading the text backward to force their brain to look at each individual word.

fun_activity.title: 🔙 The Backward Read
fun_activity.instructions: Take a short paragraph you just wrote. Instead of reading it normally, read it starting from the very last word and moving backward to the first word. Because the sentence makes no logical sense this way, your brain is forced to look at the spelling of every single word. You will instantly spot typos!

exam_tips: 📌 Never rely entirely on computer spellcheckers. Always emphasize the necessity of human proofreading in your exam answers.
📌 Know standard proofreading marks if they are covered in your syllabus (like the caret symbol `^` to insert a word, or crossing out a letter to delete it).
📌 Proofreading requires a 'fresh set of eyes'. Always advise taking a break between writing a piece and proofreading it.
quick_recap: ⭐ Editing improves the quality of the writing; Proofreading ensures its accuracy.
⭐ The most common errors are often the smallest: misplaced commas, missing articles (a/an/the), and homophone mix-ups.
⭐ Consistency is key. If you spell a word one way on page 1, it must be spelled the exact same way on page 10.
